CHIEF COMPLAINT
Severe right upper arm pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female presents with severe right upper arm pain following a volleyball injury sustained approximately 18 hours ago. Patient reports she was playing volleyball at 7:00 PM last night when an opponent kicked her legs from under her as she was attempting to spike the ball, causing her to fall and land on her right arm/shoulder. Pain is severe, rated 9/10. Patient has been taking ibuprofen every 6 hours with minimal relief. Denies use of ice therapy.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies numbness or tingling in right arm.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Gallstones
2. Lumbar fusion (6 years ago)

MEDICATIONS
1. Pepcid
2. Ibuprofen

ALLERGIES
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY
Not reported

SOCIAL HISTORY
Plays recreational volleyball

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right arm and shoulder with swelling and erythema. Tenderness over right shoulder. Able to straighten elbow without shoulder movement. Normal elbow flexion/extension. Normal pulses. No sensory deficits. Rest of body normal.

RESULTS
X-ray of right arm: Proximal humerus fracture

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Proximal humerus fracture. Conservative management with long arm cast and sling. Follow-up imaging in 2 weeks to assess bone alignment. If bones have not realigned, will discuss surgical intervention at that time. Prescribed Lortab 5 mg, 1-2 tablets every 6 hours as needed for pain (20 tablets).
